newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela studies launch of new flagship airline.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela studies launch of new flagship airline.

text.p: The Venezuelan government announced Monday it had created a commssion to study the creation of a new flagship airline following last week's decision to liquidate international carrier Viasa.

"We started working on the project at the weekend and the commission will define if VIASA workers are needed to participate," Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) President Alberto Polletto told reporters.
The FIV - the government body responsible for privatization - and Spanish airline Iberia decided last Thursday to liquidate Viasa which has debts of more than $150 million.
Viasa's 2,250 workers opposed the liquidation but have said they would be interested in taking an equity stake in a new airline.
"The reincorporation of all VIASA workers is not planned in the project for the new airline but it would be an alternative...for many of them," Poletto said.
Poletto noted that Viasa's routes that linked the Venezuelan capital with other Latin American countries, the United States and western Europe, belong to the Venezuelan government.
If the commission decides that a the new airline project is viable domestic and international investors will be invited to come up with a concrete proposal before the end of the year, he said.
